backlog.spec: For half of the non-guided restarts (chosen with the seed rng), replace the uniform random centres by a jittered grid: pick (rows, cols) at random from [(6, 6), (5, 7), (7, 5), (6, 5) plus 2 extras, (4, 8), (8, 4)], lay out cell-centred grid points in the unit square, shift every other row by half a cell with probability 0.5, select exactly n points at random (if the grid has fewer than n points, add uniform random points to reach n), and add normal jitter with sd 0.25 of the cell size, clipped to [0.02, 0.98]. The other half keep uniform starts and the guided restarts are unchanged. A fixed jittered grid looked promising in slot 6; this varies the row structure so that restarts cover several plausible layouts.
backlog.title: Random-shape jittered grid starts under the guided scheme

backlog.spec: Raise TIME_FRACTION from 0.8 to 0.92, and guard against overrun: record the CPU time of the slowest restart so far, and stop the loop when the time remaining before 0.97 * time_limit is less than 1.5 times that slowest duration. The guided phase still starts at 0.5 * TIME_FRACTION * time_limit. This gives roughly 15 percent more restarts per call while staying far below the 45 s void limit.
backlog.title: Use more of the time limit with a deadline-aware last restart

backlog.spec: Restructure solve into two phases. Phase 1 (first 55 percent of the time): run restarts with a low SLSQP maxiter (about 60) and keep the top 5 results by repaired sum of radii in a list, de-duplicated by requiring a sum difference of more than 1e-6. Phase 2 (until 85 percent of the time): for each kept candidate in order of quality, restart SLSQP from its exact centres and radii (no noise) with maxiter 1000 and ftol 1e-12, repair, and keep the overall best. Add a maxiter and an x0 argument to _solve_once to support this. Check the clock before each polish and stop if the remaining time is less than twice the longest SLSQP call seen so far, so the 45 s limit is never at risk.
backlog.title: Two-stage restarts: cheap screening then polish of the top few

backlog.spec: In guided restarts, replace the independent per-circle normal jitter by a smooth low-frequency displacement field so that neighbouring circles move together: draw amplitudes a (shape (2, 2, 2), normal with sd 0.03), integer frequencies kx, ky in {1, 2} and phases in [0, 2*pi) from the seed rng, and set displacement_d(c) = sum over 2 terms of a[d, t, 0] * sin(2*pi*(kx*c_x + ky*c_y) + phase) for d in {x, y}. Add this to the best centres, plus a small independent jitter with sd 0.005, clip to [0, 1], then run SLSQP as now. This shears and compresses whole regions of the packing instead of scrambling local contacts.
backlog.title: Smooth collective displacement field for guided restarts

backlog.spec: Keep the current guided-restart logic unchanged. For non-guided restarts only, insert a pre-stage in _solve_once before the free-radius SLSQP: optimise the variables (2n centres, one shared radius R) to maximise R subject to pairwise distance >= 2R and wall distance >= R, with SLSQP, maxiter 60, starting from the uniform random centres and R = 0.03. Then use the resulting centres as the start of the existing free-radius SLSQP (radii initialised to INIT_RADIUS as now). Guided restarts (init is not None) skip the pre-stage. This is the slot 27 idea, which was only tested without competing against the guided restarts in the same file; the goal is to check whether the two gains stack.
backlog.title: Equal-radius pre-stage stacked on the guided restarts

backlog.spec: Reduce the SLSQP constraint count from 496 pair constraints to only near pairs. In _solve_once, run SLSQP in rounds: at the start of each round compute the pair list of circles whose centre distance is below 0.45 (always include at least each circle's 8 nearest neighbours), build cons using only those pairs plus the wall and r >= 0 constraints, and run SLSQP for up to 60 iterations; repeat for up to 4 rounds, rebuilding the pair list from the current centres, and stop early when a round changes the objective by less than 1e-9. The existing _repair over all pairs remains as the validity guard, so a rare violated far pair is still corrected. Fewer constraints make each SLSQP iteration and its QP subproblem several times cheaper, giving more restarts and deeper convergence.
backlog.title: Active-set constraint pruning by neighbour list

backlog.spec: Keep a small elite pool of the 4 best distinct packings (centres and radii) instead of a single best. After the first 40 percent of the time, generate half of the new starts by crossover: pick two elites with rng, apply a random symmetry of the square (one of the 8 rotations/reflections) to the second, choose a random vertical or horizontal cut position in [0.35, 0.65], take the circles of the first parent on one side of the cut and those of the second parent on the other side, then drop the smallest or duplicate the largest-clearance random points until exactly n circles remain. Start radii at 0.85 times the parents' values, run SLSQP, repair, and insert into the pool if it beats the worst elite and its sum differs from all elites by more than 1e-7. The other half of the starts remain random restarts.
backlog.title: Symmetry-and-swap population of elites with crossover restarts

backlog.spec: Guided restarts start close to a local optimum and should not need 200 SLSQP iterations. Add a setting GUIDED_MAX_ITER = 80 and use it as maxiter when init is not None; non-guided restarts keep MAX_ITER = 200. This roughly doubles the number of guided attempts in the second half of the budget at no cost to the random restarts.
backlog.title: Shorter iteration cap for guided restarts

backlog.spec: In cons, replace the pairwise constraint sqrt(dist2) - r_i - r_j >= 0 by the smooth form dist2 - (r_i + r_j)**2 >= 0 (no square root). It is differentiable when centres coincide and gives SLSQP a different, better-scaled linearisation with finite differences. Keep the wall and r >= 0 constraints and _repair unchanged (the repair still uses true distances, so validity is unaffected).
backlog.title: Squared-distance form of the non-overlap constraints

backlog.spec: Change the unguided initial centres in _solve_once from uniform random to structured staggered-row layouts. Using rng, pick a row pattern at random from a small list of row counts summing to 32 (for example [6,5,6,5,6,4], [6,6,5,5,5,5], [5,6,5,6,5,5], [6,5,5,6,5,5], [7,6,7,6,6], [6,7,6,7,6]); place rows at evenly spaced y in (0,1), each row's circles evenly spaced in x with alternating rows offset by half a spacing, then add Gaussian jitter with sd about 0.02 and clip to [0.03, 0.97]. Randomly transpose x and y half the time. Use uniform random init for about 30 percent of the restarts for diversity. Set the initial radius to roughly 0.4 times the typical spacing. Rationale: good packings of 32 circles are near-hexagonal with a few defects, and SLSQP from uniform random starts rarely reaches those basins.
backlog.title: Hexagonal-like row initialisations with jitter
